nodes.label: atomicity
nodes.def: The all-or-nothing property: a transaction's effects are either fully applied or fully absent; implemented via undo_log and transaction rollback.

nodes.label: isolation level
nodes.def: A configurable parameter defining the degree to which concurrent transactions are isolated from each other's uncommitted or intermediate effects.

nodes.label: rollback
nodes.def: The act of undoing a transaction's effects using undo_log entries, returning the database to its pre-transaction state.

nodes.label: tl log record
nodes.def: The fundamental unit of a transaction_log: a single append-only entry recording one atomic change or lifecycle event made by a transaction; identified by an lsn.

nodes.label: read committed
nodes.def: An isolation_level where each statement sees only data committed before that statement begins; prevents dirty_read but allows non_repeatable_read and phantom_read.

nodes.label: row level locking
nodes.def: Lock management at the individual row granularity via row_lock entries in lock_manager's lock table; enables high concurrency but increases lock_manager overhead.

nodes.label: transaction state
nodes.def: The current phase of a transaction lifecycle: active, partially_committed, committed, aborted; drives lock release and recovery behavior.

nodes.label: acid properties
nodes.def: The four guarantees of database transactions: atomicity, consistency, isolation, durability — the foundational contract between a DBMS and its clients.

nodes.label: commit
nodes.def: The act of making a transaction's effects permanent: flush log records to durable storage, release locks, transition transaction_state to committed.

nodes.label: concurrency control
nodes.def: The set of mechanisms a DBMS uses to manage simultaneous access to shared data while preserving correctness and isolation guarantees.

nodes.label: database transaction
nodes.def: A logical unit of work executed against a database, bounded by BEGIN and COMMIT/ROLLBACK, guaranteeing ACID properties across one or more SQL operations.

nodes.label: dirty read
nodes.def: An anomaly where a transaction reads data written by another transaction that has not yet committed; only possible in read_uncommitted.

nodes.label: commit visibility boundary
nodes.def: temporal threshold in read_committed: a datum is visible iff its committing_transaction committed before the reading statement started

nodes.label: committed data
nodes.def: database state resulting from successfully completed transactions; constitutes the visible universe for read_committed queries

nodes.label: exclusive lock
nodes.def: A lock type granting sole read-write access to a resource; incompatible with all other lock types including shared_lock and update_lock.

nodes.label: undo log
nodes.def: Log records describing the previous state of modified data; used to undo uncommitted transaction changes during rollback and recovery.

nodes.label: write ahead logging
nodes.def: A protocol requiring log records be flushed to durable storage before the corresponding data changes are applied; ensures durability and atomicity.

nodes.label: write lock held until commit
nodes.def: exclusive lock discipline in read_committed requiring a transaction to hold write locks on modified rows until transaction commit or rollback

nodes.label: before image
nodes.def: The committed database state of a row immediately before a transaction modifies it; recorded in the undo_log so the modification can be undone if the transaction rolls back.

nodes.label: committed
nodes.def: The terminal transaction_state after durable persistence of all changes; locks are released per locking_protocol rules.

nodes.label: lock granularity
nodes.def: The size of the database object protected by a lock: row_lock, page_lock, table_lock — trading off concurrency against lock_manager overhead.

nodes.label: read uncommitted
nodes.def: The weakest isolation_level: transactions may observe uncommitted changes from other transactions, permitting dirty_read.

nodes.label: statement
nodes.def: A single SQL operation within a transaction; atomicity requires that each statement either fully completes its effect or fully reverts before the next statement begins.

nodes.label: statement level read consistency
nodes.def: guarantee within read_committed that each SQL statement sees all changes committed at the moment that statement began execution

nodes.label: tl checkpoint record
nodes.def: A special log_record written periodically by a checkpoint_writer; records the volatile database state at a consistent point, bounding the recovery_manager's replay horizon.

nodes.label: tl undo log
nodes.def: A structured collection of tl_update_record entries chained by a transaction; traversed in reverse order during rollback to restore the before_image of each modified entity.

nodes.label: tl update record
nodes.def: A log_record capturing a before_image and after_image of a modified data page or row; used by both redo_recovery (for durability) and undo_recovery (for atomicity rollback).

nodes.label: transaction boundary
nodes.def: The demarcation point between consecutive transaction executions defining the scope over which atomicity applies; all effects within are committed or none are, with no partial visi

nodes.label: transaction log
nodes.def: An append-only sequence of records tracking every change made by transactions; the primary mechanism for atomicity and durability.

nodes.label: two phase locking
nodes.def: A locking_protocol where transactions must acquire all locks during a growing_phase and release all locks during a shrinking_phase, guaranteeing conflict_serializable schedules.

nodes.label: uncommitted change
nodes.def: A modification to database state made by a transaction that has not yet committed; visible to other transactions at read_uncommitted.

nodes.label: aborted state
nodes.def: The terminal transaction_state after rollback completes; all acquired locks are released and the transaction cannot be restarted automatically.

nodes.label: all or nothing
nodes.def: The conceptual guarantee that a transaction executes as an indivisible unit: either every operation succeeds or no operation has any effect.

nodes.label: consistency
nodes.def: A transaction transforms the database from one valid state to another, preserving all defined integrity constraints and business rules.

nodes.label: isolation
nodes.def: The property that concurrently executing transactions do not interfere with each other; the degree of interference is controlled by isolation_level.

nodes.label: lock timeout handling
nodes.def: timeout mechanism in read_committed for transactions blocked waiting to acquire conflicting locks on rows

nodes.label: locking protocol
nodes.def: A disciplined set of rules governing when locks may be acquired and released to ensure serializability or other isolation guarantees.

nodes.label: no dirty reads
nodes.def: the guaranteed anomaly prevention in read_committed: a transaction may never observe uncommitted changes from concurrent transactions

nodes.label: non repeatable read possible
nodes.def: the permitted anomaly in read_committed: a transaction reading the same row twice may observe different values if a concurrent transaction updates and commits that row between read

nodes.label: optimistic cc
nodes.def: Concurrency control strategy that permits unrestricted execution and detects conflicts only at validation_phase, aborting and retrying on conflict.

nodes.label: read lock release
nodes.def: lock management characteristic in read_committed where shared read locks are typically released immediately after each row access rather than held to transaction end

nodes.label: serializable
nodes.def: The strongest isolation_level: the result of executing concurrent transactions is equivalent to some serial order of those transactions; prevents all anomalies.

nodes.label: statement start timestamp
nodes.def: logical moment recorded when each statement begins, establishing the visibility cutoff point for read_committed row versions

nodes.label: strict two phase locking
nodes.def: A variant of two_phase_locking where exclusive_locks are held until transaction end, ensuring strict_schedule and enabling cascading_less schedules.

nodes.label: timestamp ordering
nodes.def: A concurrency control method assigning timestamps to transactions and using them to order operations, ensuring serializability without locking.

nodes.label: tl abort record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction enters the aborted_state; signals that undo_log entries must be applied to reverse this transaction's effects.

nodes.label: tl checkpoint writer
nodes.def: The subsystem component that periodically writes a tl_checkpoint_record to the transaction_log; trims obsolete log segments and bounds crash_recovery time.

nodes.label: tl commit record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction commits; marks the durable persistence boundary for durability guarantees; flushed to disk before the transaction releases its locks.

nodes.def: A runtime data structure maintained by recovery_manager listing data pages modified but not yet flushed; consulted during checkpoint to ensure write_ahead_logging invariants hold.

nodes.label: transaction read
nodes.def: The act of a transaction executing a read operation; at read_uncommitted this read may return uncommitted_change from concurrent transactions.

nodes.label: update lock
nodes.def: A lock type that prevents deadlock during lock_upgrade: compatible with shared_lock but not with other update_locks or exclusive_locks.

nodes.label: write lock not required
nodes.def: The characteristic of read_uncommitted where a writing transaction does not hold an exclusive lock preventing other transactions from reading its uncommitted state.

nodes.label: active state
nodes.def: The initial transaction_state: transaction is executing, holding locks, accumulating changes in transaction_log.

nodes.label: advisory lock
nodes.def: An application-defined lock with no automatic database effect; the application is responsible for enforcing its meaning and usage pattern.

nodes.label: after image
nodes.def: The state of a row resulting from a transaction's modification; stored for redo in write_ahead_logging systems to guarantee durability alongside atomicity.

nodes.label: aries recovery
nodes.def: The Algorithm for Recovery and Isolation Exploiting Semantics: a precise recovery procedure using transaction_log, undo_log, and redo_log to achieve atomicity and durability.

nodes.label: auto commit
nodes.def: A mode where each individual SQL statement is implicitly wrapped in its own transaction, committing immediately upon statement completion.

nodes.label: basic timestamp protocol
nodes.def: A timestamp_ordering scheme where each data item maintains read_timestamp and write_timestamp; transactions violating these abort.

nodes.label: cap theorem
nodes.def: A theorem stating that a distributed system can provide at most two of three properties: consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

nodes.label: cascadeless schedule
nodes.def: A recoverable_schedule where transactions only read data committed before the transaction began; prevents cascading aborts.

nodes.label: causal consistency
nodes.def: A consistency model guaranteeing that causally related operations appear in order across all nodes; weaker than strong_consistency but stronger than eventual_consistency_level.

nodes.label: checkpoint
nodes.def: A consistent point-in-time snapshot of the database state written to durable storage, reducing recovery time by bounding how far recovery must replay logs.

nodes.label: clip xmin
nodes.def: The oldest active transaction_id below which all row versions are guaranteed visible to all current transactions.

nodes.label: committed before statement
nodes.def: A temporal boundary condition: only modifications committed before the statement_start are visible; uncommitted changes are invisible.

nodes.label: committed version
nodes.def: The state of a row or data item after its modifying transaction has committed, making it visible to concurrent read_committed statements.

nodes.label: compare and swap
nodes.def: An atomic primitive that atomically compares a memory value with an expected value and swaps it if equal; used in lock_free_cc for conflict-free updates.

nodes.label: compare and swap pattern
nodes.def: An optimistic_cc pattern using compare_and_swap on a version or sequence number to detect concurrent modifications without locking.

nodes.label: compensating transaction
nodes.def: A reverse operation executed to undo the effects of a saga step when a subsequent step fails, restoring the system to a consistent state.

nodes.label: compensation
nodes.def: The compensatory action taken to reverse a transaction's effects, encompassing rollback via undo_log as the primary compensation mechanism.

nodes.label: concurrency level
nodes.def: A configuration parameter (often database pool size) controlling the maximum number of concurrent transactions or connections.

nodes.label: conflict detection
nodes.def: The mechanism in optimistic_cc determining whether a transaction's read_set or write_set overlaps with another transaction's write_set in a forbidden way.

nodes.label: conflict serializable
nodes.def: A schedule property where serializability can be proven by analyzing the conflict graph of read/write operations; achievable with strict_two_phase_locking.

nodes.label: conservative two phase locking
nodes.def: A variant of two_phase_locking where all locks are acquired before the transaction begins, eliminating deadlock entirely at the cost of reduced concurrency.

nodes.label: durability
nodes.def: Once a transaction commits, its effects persist permanently even after system crash; guaranteed by write_ahead_logging and recovery_manager.

nodes.label: eventual consistency
nodes.def: A consistency model where updates propagate asynchronously and all replicas converge to the same state given no new updates; relevant in distributed_transaction.

nodes.label: lock contention
nodes.def: A performance condition where many transactions compete for the same locks, causing lock_wait and degrading throughput; mitigated by lock_granularity tuning.

nodes.label: lock upgrade
nodes.def: The conversion of a held shared_lock to an exclusive_lock; requires checking lock_compatibility_matrix and may block or fail if incompatible locks exist.

nodes.label: mvcc
nodes.def: Multi-version concurrency control: maintain multiple versions of rows so readers and writers do not block each other, each transaction sees a snapshot.

nodes.label: non repeatable read
nodes.def: An anomaly where a transaction reads the same row twice and gets different values because another transaction modified and committed between reads.

nodes.label: observation window
nodes.def: The temporal scope during which a reading transaction may see uncommitted changes from other transactions, bounded by those transactions' commit operations.

nodes.label: page lock
nodes.def: A lock_granularity unit protecting a disk page (typically 4–16 KB); intermediate granularity used in some storage engines.

nodes.label: pessimistic cc
nodes.def: Concurrency control strategy that prevents conflicts by acquiring locks before accessing data, blocking if locks are unavailable.

nodes.label: phantom read
nodes.def: An anomaly where a transaction re-executes a range query and gets a different set of rows due to another transaction inserting or deleting rows in that range.

nodes.label: recovery manager
nodes.def: The component responsible for restoring database consistency after failure using transaction_log and ARIES_recovery.

nodes.label: repeatable read
nodes.def: An isolation_level ensuring that all reads within a transaction see a consistent snapshot as of transaction start; prevents non_repeatable_read but may permit phantom_read.

nodes.label: row lock
nodes.def: A lock_granularity unit protecting a single row; maximum concurrency but highest lock_manager overhead and risk of lock_contention.

nodes.label: shared lock
nodes.def: A lock type permitting concurrent reads by multiple transactions but preventing exclusive writes; compatible with other shared_locks, incompatible with exclusive_lock.

nodes.label: snapshot isolation
nodes.def: An isolation_level using mvcc where a transaction reads from a consistent snapshot taken at transaction start; prevents lost_update but allows write_skew.

nodes.label: strict schedule
nodes.def: A schedule where reads and writes of a data item occur in the same order as in a serial schedule; required for strict_two_phase_locking and ARIES recovery.

nodes.label: strong strict two phase locking
nodes.def: strict_two_phase_locking where all locks (shared and exclusive) are held until transaction end, the most common production locking_protocol.

nodes.label: table lock
nodes.def: A lock_granularity unit protecting an entire table; high lock_manager efficiency but low concurrency for partitioned or sparse tables.

nodes.label: tl begin record
nodes.def: A log_record written when a transaction transitions to the active transaction_state; records transaction_id and start timestamp but no data modifications.

nodes.label: tl log buffer

nodes.label: transaction id
nodes.def: A monotonically increasing identifier assigned to each transaction; the basis for snapshot_isolation read_view construction and visibility_check.

nodes.label: uncommitted version
nodes.def: The state of a row or data item modified by an active uncommitted transaction, invisible to read_committed statements.

nodes.label: connection pool limiting
nodes.def: A concurrency control mechanism restricting the number of concurrent database connections to bound resource usage and lock_contention.

nodes.label: consensus protocol
nodes.def: A distributed algorithm enabling distributed_transaction participants to agree on a single value or decision; used alongside two_phase_commit for fault tolerance.

nodes.label: cursor stability
nodes.def: An isolation_level specific to cursor-based reads: locks are held only on the current row, providing a middle ground between read_uncommitted and read_committed.

nodes.label: database pool exhaustion
nodes.def: A failure condition where all connections in a connection_pool are consumed by blocked transactions waiting for locks, preventing new transactions from starting.

nodes.label: deadlock
nodes.def: A cycle of transactions each waiting to acquire a lock held by the next transaction in the cycle, causing all involved transactions to block indefinitely.

nodes.label: deadlock detection
nodes.def: The process of identifying when a deadlock has formed, typically via a wait_for_graph analyzed by lock_manager.

nodes.label: deadlock detection interval
nodes.def: The frequency with which lock_manager runs deadlock detection; shorter intervals catch deadlocks faster at higher CPU cost.

nodes.label: deadlock frequency
nodes.def: The rate at which deadlocks occur in the system; indicates whether deadlock_prevention or deadlock_detection thresholds need tuning.

nodes.label: deadlock prevention
nodes.def: Protocols that ensure deadlocks cannot occur by ordering lock acquisition or assigning priorities that determine which transaction rolls back.

nodes.label: dirty write
nodes.def: An anomaly where one transaction overwrites an uncommitted value written by another transaction, violating atomicity and potentially causing inconsistency.

nodes.label: distributed locking
nodes.def: Lock management across multiple database nodes using a distributed lock service; required for distributed_transaction coordination.

nodes.label: distributed transaction
nodes.def: A transaction spanning multiple database nodes or storage systems; requires coordination protocols like two_phase_commit for atomicity.

nodes.label: eventual consistency level
nodes.def: A consistency model where reads may return stale data but the system guarantees convergence after all writes propagate and settle.

nodes.label: exponential backoff
nodes.def: A retry strategy where the delay before each transaction_retry doubles exponentially, reducing contention and thundering herd on shared resources.

nodes.label: for update nowait
nodes.def: A select_for_update variant that fails immediately if any requested lock cannot be acquired rather than blocking.

nodes.label: for update skip locked
nodes.def: A select_for_update variant that skips rows already locked by other transactions, returning only rows that can be locked immediately.

nodes.label: frozen xid
nodes.def: A special transaction_id older than all normal transaction_ids; row versions with frozen_xid are always visible and never garbage collected.

nodes.label: consensus
nodes.def: Agreement on a single value among a set of distributed processes; the core problem consensus protocols solve.

nodes.label: quorum
nodes.def: Subset of nodes sufficient for reads or writes; typically majority (n/2+1) for strong consistency.

nodes.label: replicated log

nodes.label: client session

nodes.label: failure detection

nodes.label: failure mode

nodes.label: linearizability

nodes.label: reconfiguration

nodes.label: recovery

nodes.label: mode type bits

nodes.label: submodule pointer
